entry.note: PDF verified: Freedman, Kitaev, Larsen, Wang, "Topological Quantum Computation," Bull. AMS 40 (2003), arXiv:quant-ph/0101025. Verified.

relevance.rationale: Join CORRECT (arXiv:quant-ph/0101025v2, Freedman-Kitaev-Larsen-Wang, matching the registered entry's authors and DOI). Not in the working tree on this branch; recovered from intake commit 955885756c, sha matches. Six .ts cites sites and eight Lean sites. Load-bearing at the two that matter, with one scope slip. (a) information-theory/quantum-computational-universality.lean:30,59 cites it on the opaque Prop QuantumUniversalityHolds whose docstring says 'At level k >= 3, the braiding representation is dense in SU(2^n)'. This document does state that result - but with an exception the docstring drops: its text reads 'matrices have been shown to be universal for k >= 3, k != 4', and it attributes the proof to its own refs [8],[9] (Freedman-Larsen-Wang, Comm. Math. Phys. 227 (2002)), so it is a survey citation, not the primary source. (b) information-theory/qou-p-neq-np.md attributes 'additive approximation is BQP-complete at a primitive root of unity of order n does not divide 6' jointly to Aharonov-Jones-Landau and FKLW; this document supports the BQP side (it defines BQP and states the TQC-BQP equivalence) but the root-of-unity stratification itself comes from the AJL/JVW side, which the block also cites. (c) The remaining sites (p-vs-np-boundary.lean:30, PvsNPQou.lean:23,51, appendix-surreals cites arrays, skein-filtration-trichotomy.ts:15) are References-block mentions, background not load-bearing. Notably the block prose is scrupulous about labelling the P != NP step an analogy rather than a theorem, so nothing is being laundered here.

keyResults.locator: p. 5 (main text, near the level-k discussion)
keyResults.statement: The braid matrices for SU(2) Chern-Simons at level k have been shown to be universal for quantum computation for k >= 3, k != 4 (attributed to refs [8],[9] of the survey).
keyResults.useForFolio: Restore the k != 4 exception to the QuantumUniversalityHolds docstring, and cite the primary source (Freedman-Larsen-Wang CMP 227 (2002)) alongside the survey.

proposedActions.rationale: The Lean sub-claim states 'at level k >= 3' where the cited source states 'k >= 3, k != 4'. Restore the exception and add the primary reference; a survey citation for a density theorem should name the paper that proves it.
